cells.title: Park a cell on a question and answer it
cells.action: Add two cell verbs per contract decision 16031715 (D1 b7b5b3c7, D2 8ed6f4a2). `bee cells park --id <cell> --question <text>` sets an open or claimed cell to status `parked`, writes trace.parked_question and trace.parked_at, and refuses an empty question or a cell that is capped, dropped or already parked. `bee cells answer --id <cell> --answer <text>` refuses a cell that is not parked; otherwise it logs the answer as a decision (tags cells and answer; the decision text names the cell id and quotes the question) BEFORE it writes the cell, appends the new decision id to the cell's `decisions`, moves the question into trace.park_history (question, answer decision id, time), clears trace.parked_question, and sets status `open`. A failed decision log leaves the cell unchanged. Copy the shape of `run_block` / `block_cell` in handlers_close.rs (rg anchor: `"block" => run_block(flags, use_json, t0),` in util.rs) and of `record_dissent_verdict` in dissent.rs for log-then-write. audit.rs `log_decision` returns no id today (`pub(crate) fn log_decision(root: &Path, decision: &str, rationale: &str, tags: &[&str]) -> MR<()> {`): add a variant that returns the id; keep the old signature for its callers. Register both verbs in the util.rs try_mutating match AND in generated/registry_payload.json (the registry tests fail if a served verb is undeclared); if the registry file is produced by a regen step, run that step. Also export a reader `feature_parked_cells(root, feature) -> Vec<(cell id, question)>` from the cells module for cqp-2. Check the existing status checks for a status they now meet: handlers_write.rs `let status_ok = matches!(cell_map.get("status"), Some(Value::String(s)) if s == "open" || s == "blocked");` and `if status != "open" && status != "blocked" {` — a parked cell must not be claimable and must not be updatable into a running state; leave them unchanged unless a test shows a parked cell slips through. Tests red-first: park sets status and question; a parked cell is absent from compute_schedule's ready set while its open sibling is present; a cell that depends on a parked cell is not ready; answer logs a decision, cites it on the cell and reopens it; the refusals named above.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee -- cells registry

truths: bee cells park sets the cell status to parked and stores the question in trace.parked_question
a parked cell is not in the ready set while its open sibling is
a cell that depends on a parked cell is not ready
bee cells answer logs a decision, appends its id to the cell decisions, and sets the cell status to open
park refuses an empty question and a capped, dropped or already-parked cell; answer refuses a cell that is not parked

cells.title: Refuse close and merge on a parked cell and list it for the human
cells.action: Per contract decision 3041908c (D3 e2e0e77e, D4 2fe6f2a3), using the `feature_parked_cells` reader cqp-1 added in verbs/cells/park.rs. (1) bee close: add a door named `parked-cell` beside the dissent-debt door in drivers/close.rs (rg anchor: `let dissent = crate::verbs::cells::feature_dissent_debt(root, feature)?;`); it blocks while the feature has a parked cell and its message names every parked cell id and its question. Check both close paths that read dissent debt (close_handler reads it a second time) so a dry run and a real close agree. (2) bee worktree merge: in merge_stage in worktree/phases.rs, beside `let dissent = crate::verbs::cells::feature_dissent_debt(main_root, feature)`, refuse with code WORKTREE_MERGE_PARKED_CELL before any write, naming every parked cell and its question. (3) supervisor.rs collect_needs_you: after the waiting-on row (`if let Some((kind, subject)) = live_waiting_on(control) {`), add one ReportItem per parked cell across live features, text naming the cell id and the clipped question. Tests red-first: close refuses with the parked-cell door; merge refuses with WORKTREE_MERGE_PARKED_CELL and writes nothing (copy the write_dissenting_cell fixture style in worktree/tests.rs); the needs-you view lists a parked cell; after answer reopens the cell, the door and the refusal no longer fire for parking.
cells.verify: cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml -p bee -- close worktree supervisor

truths: bee close blocks on a door named parked-cell that names each parked cell id and question
bee worktree merge refuses with WORKTREE_MERGE_PARKED_CELL before any write
the supervisor what-needs-you view lists one row per parked cell with its question
a feature with no parked cell closes and merges as before
key_links: close.rs and phases.rs both call feature_parked_cells
prohibitions: Do not change the dissent-debt door or refusal

cells.title: Teach workers to park and leaders to keep working
cells.action: Doctrine for D1, D2 and D3. In skills/bee-swarming/SKILL.md (the worker contract, section Execute): a worker with a product question it cannot answer runs `bee cells park --id <cell> --question "<question>"` and returns [BLOCKED]; it never stops the lane. On the leader side: when a worker parks, the leader keeps dispatching ready cells; it sets `bee state waiting-on set --kind question` only when no ready cell remains in the lane, and lists every open parked question in its reply; the human's answer is recorded with `bee cells answer --id <cell> --answer "<text>"`, and the cell runs again with the answer in its brief. In skills/bee-hive/references/gates-and-delegation.md, where the waiting-on mark and questions are described, add one line that points to this rule (one home: the swarming skill). Keep each addition short. Then run the regen chain (`bee dev regen`) so rendered skill trees and the release manifest follow, and run the manifest check.

truths: the worker contract tells a worker with a question to park its cell, not stop the lane
the leader rule sets the waiting-on question mark only when no ready cell remains
the answer path names bee cells answer
key_links: gates-and-delegation.md points to the swarming rule
prohibitions: Do not restate the rule in a second home
